details:
* This is the first ELS release of unbound for xenial. It also carries
     the fixes of the entries els1 to els5 below; their CVEs are listed
     here again so that the advisory names all of them.
   * SECURITY UPDATE: harden compressed name copies against heap corruption
     - debian/patches/CVE-2026-82717.patch: restore the buffer position
       when a compressed name fails to parse in util/data/dname.c and
       check every decompressed name and rdata copy against the allocated
       size in util/data/msgreply.c; add testdata/dname_pkt_alter.rpl.
       Hardening: 1.5.8 does not write into the packet during CNAME
       synthesis, which is the trigger of this issue.
     - CVE-2026-82717
   * SECURITY UPDATE: CPU exhaustion via DNSSEC validation (ReTrap)
     - debian/patches/CVE-2026-85501.patch (els5)
     - CVE-2026-85501
   * SECURITY UPDATE: cache poisoning via per-thread source port ranges
     - debian/patches/CVE-2026-50252.patch (els5)
     - CVE-2026-50252
   * SECURITY UPDATE: CPU exhaustion via DNSSEC validation (KeyTrap)
     - debian/patches/CVE-2023-50387.patch (els4)
     - CVE-2023-50387
   * SECURITY UPDATE: CPU exhaustion via NSEC3 closest encloser proofs
     - debian/patches/CVE-2023-50868.patch (els4)
     - CVE-2023-50868
   * SECURITY UPDATE: heap buffer overflow when digesting a DNSKEY
     - debian/patches/CVE-2026-81642.patch (els3)
     - CVE-2026-81642
   * SECURITY UPDATE: cache poisoning via address records for non-NS
     authority RRsets
     - debian/patches/CVE-2026-42960.patch (els3)
     - CVE-2026-42960
   * SECURITY UPDATE: wrong additional-section offsets in the DNSSEC
     validator
     - debian/patches/CVE-2026-42959.patch (els3)
     - CVE-2026-42959
   * SECURITY UPDATE: heap buffer overflow in DNSSEC canonicalization
     - debian/patches/CVE-2026-81634.patch (els3)
     - CVE-2026-81634
   * SECURITY UPDATE: assertion failure in synth_cname
